question.prompt:
A semicircle is inscribed in an isosceles triangle with base \(16\) and height \(15\) so that the diameter of the semicircle is contained in the base of the triangle as shown. What is the radius of the semicircle?

[Figure 1](figures/2016_AMC_8_Q25_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The useful observation is that a radius to a tangency point is perpendicular to the tangent side. This lets us use the radius as a height in an area calculation.

Let \(A\) be the apex and \(B,C\) the base endpoints. Draw the altitude \(AM\). In an isosceles triangle, this altitude bisects the base, so \(BM=CM=8\) and \(AM=15\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
AB=AC=\sqrt{8^2+15^2}=17.
\]
Let \(O\) be the semicircle's center and \(r>0\) its radius. Because its diameter lies on \(BC\), the center \(O\) lies on \(BC\). Both sloping sides are tangent to the semicircle, so the perpendicular distance from \(O\) to each sloping side is \(r\).

Joining \(A\) to \(O\) splits the whole triangle into \(ABO\) and \(ACO\). Each has a sloping side of length \(17\) as a base and corresponding height \(r\). Equating their combined area to the area of the whole triangle gives
\[
\frac12(16)(15)=\frac12(17)r+\frac12(17)r.
\]
Thus \(120=17r\), so the radius is \(\boxed{\dfrac{120}{17}}\), choice B.
solutions.title: Use the radius as a triangle height
